text:
alex.gonzalez: Hey team — customers are hitting a lot of 429s on production since ~09:12 UTC when prefetching long-context documents into rwd-extended. Response headers show x-rate-limit-remaining: 0 and x-rate-limit-reset: 33. They were fanouting 12 concurrent requests with ~48k context.

marta: @alex.gonzalez can you paste a minimal repro curl? Also which model variant are they calling (exact model string)?

alex.gonzalez: Sure — they call `rwd-extended-v1` (not tuned for high concurrency). Repro curl:```curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-extended-v1","input":"<huge-prompt>","max_tokens":512}'``` We also see spikes in auth latency ~300ms then 429.

jordan: Sounds like per-model RPM/TPM + concurrency ceiling + long-context KL is interacting. Do we have the per-org per-model numbers for this tier?

support-bot: Notice: org org-84 hit per-model throughput cap. Suggested: exponential backoff + jitter, reduce concurrent workers, or route to a compatible lower-context variant.

marta: Quick numbers for this customer tier: rough ballpark for rwd-extended-v1 on hosted tier -> RPM ~400, TPM ~9k, max_concurrency 6, context_limit 65536. If you fanout 12 concurrent requests with 48k each, you can blow both concurrency and TPM. (we'll validate exact account quotas offline).

kevin: Repro steps I used locally: 1) spawn 12 parallel curl processes with the payload above; 2) observe ~50% 429s within 30s; 3) capture response headers: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 400`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 28`. I included the shell loop:```for i in {1..12}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-extended-v1","input":"A... (48k)"}' & done; wait```

alex.gonzalez: We also tried switching to `rwd-stream-small-v1` (lower context, higher concurrency) and 429s dropped but quality is worse. Any suggestions other than raising quota?

marta: Options: 1) Reduce parallel clients to <=6 for this model. 2) Batch multiple requests where possible (prefix caching). 3) Use a variant with higher concurrency/shorter context for prefetching then stitch server-side. 4) Apply exponential backoff on 429 with randomized jitter per RFC. 5) For sustained spikes, request a Dedicated/reserved capacity quote.

jordan: Also check prefetch pattern — if each prefetch hits full 48k context, the token TPM cost is huge (context tokens count toward TPM). Prefetching should be throttled or paginated.

kevin: Flagged an auth anomaly: some 429s had `x-auth-latency-ms: 310` which pushed requests past internal concurrency windows causing additional queueing. SRE says auth slow path can amplify bursting.

sre-ops: We're looking at auth path traces. Short-term mitigation: enable client-side concurrency cap and soft backoff (we can provide a small middleware snippet). Long-term: we'll tune the auth cache TTL for this org.

marta: For the customer, I recommended these immediate steps: 1) throttle to 4 concurrent prefetches; 2) switch prefetch to smaller windows (16k chunks) and reuse cached KV prefix; 3) implement 429 handler: `sleep = base * 2**retries + random(0, jitter)` up to 30s. I included a minimal node snippet:```async function handle429(fn){let base=250; for(let i=0;i<6;i++){try{return await fn()}catch(e){if(e.status===429){await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, base*Math.pow(2,i)+Math.random()*1000));continue}throw e}} throw new Error('too many retries')} ```

alex.gonzalez: Customer tried the throttle to 4 and 429s dropped to near zero. Thanks. They still want to know if we can temporarily raise their per-model TPM while they migrate to a better pattern.

marta: I opened an internal ticket to review quota bump for org-84 and linked usage traces. If approved we can grant a 30d temporary uplift or propose Dedicated. I'll update here once ops confirms. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: Ticket created: SUP-4331. Assigned to eng-quotas.

kevin: One follow-up: logging suggestion — capture `x-rate-limit-*` headers and `x-request-id` when a 429 occurs and include those in support tickets. Makes diagnosis & temporary bump decisions much faster.

alex.gonzalez: Will send a repro package with headers + request ids. Thanks everyone — mitigation worked, awaiting quota review. :pray:
